page.layout: One page of running text in a single column. Page number top right. Running head top centre. A centred italic heading stands between the two paragraphs. Right and bottom edges show a neighbouring page and show-through, which are left out. No marginal notes.

main_text.p: proprie ψήφισμα dicebatur, quod ante [illegible, ~10 letters] erat. Et hæc ratio duravit, quandiu civitati liberæ esse licuit.

head.i: Magistratuum & honorum capiendorum jus cum plebe communicatum.

main_text.p: Interea Solonis illa lex, quâ plebs à petendis annuis honoribus arcebatur, quæ eam velut nota quædam ignominiæ perpetuæ urebat, abrogata fuit, & jus quartæ classis cum cæteris exæquatum. Accidisse hoc, subinnuit Aristoteles eo loco, quem pluries jam laudavi; expressè autem docet Plutarchus in Aristide, statim post Persas Xerxeo tempore è Græciâ profligatos, autore præcipuo ipso Aristide. Sic enim scribit hic:

p.i: Cum plebs Attica, cujus promptâ ac fi-deli opera & fortibus aufis tanta mari terraque potissimum gesta erant, ex prælio Platæensi, in quo cornu alterum[?] tenens duce Aristide fortissimè pugna-verat, hostemque sibi oppositum latissimè ceciderat, victrix domum redisset, animos extulit, & pertæsa conditionis suæ hactenus tolerata popularem statum, sublato scilicet classium discrimine inviso & jure omnium æquato prehendere meditata fuit. Et significat Aristoteles

page.notes: The Greek word after "ante" is unreadable at this scan; the first Greek word is read as ψήφισμα with some doubt. "alterum" is partly obscured at the line end and is marked [?]. The heading is set in italic, so it is marked as a level 2 heading. The paragraph at the foot continues on the next page. The "Interea" initial is a large letter, copied as a plain capital I. The line-end hyphens "fi-" and "pugna-" are printed.
